message:
The bare bridge rings because its first bending mode has almost no damping.

Serviceability and Crowd Loading Specialist, please confirm the comfort target still stands at peak vertical acceleration 0.7 m/s squared, about 0.071 g, per the Assessment of human-induced vibrations of a cable-stayed footbridge (E1) and the A Review of Evaluation Methods of Standards for Structural Vibration Serviceability under Crowd Walking (E2), and bare steel damping near 0.4 percent of critical per the Vibration analysis of footbridges: an overview of the current practice (E4).

A Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), a sprung mass that moves out of phase with the deck to pull energy out at resonance, can add that damping without changing the deck look. The Den Hartog sizing (E11) following the Control of Vibrations of Common Pedestrian Bridges in Jordan Using Tuned Mass Dampers (E7) and the TMD_nscm19.dvi (E9) gives moving mass 800 kg, about ten adults, tuning frequency 1.83 Hz, damper ratio 12.0 percent and spring stiffness 105,000 N/m for an assumed 20,000 kg modal mass at 1.90 Hz with 4.00 percent mass ratio.

Retrofit and Maintenance Engineer and Under-Deck Integration Designer, note the load path stays hidden below the deck. The midspan TMD layout sketch (E12) shows primary longitudinal girders to transverse cross-beams to bolted support frame to coil springs plus viscous damper plus moving mass, with the frame locked to the girder bottom flange and the mass free only vertically. Not ready, because crowd force and modal mass still need confirmation before mass and stroke can freeze.
